intended_object: The shuffle sign ε(i, s) ∈ {±1}: the sign of the permutation that sorts the sequence (i, followed by the increasing enumeration of s∖{i}). When i ∈ s this is the sign of moving i to the front of s, i.e. (−1)^{#{j ∈ s : j < i}}. This reading comes from the docstring and from the lemma right after the definition.
explanation:
The body applies the private helper `basisEraseSignOfErase` to `i` and `s.erase i`. The helper takes the sign of Mathlib's `Set.powersetCard.permOfDisjoint` for the singleton {i} and the set t = s.erase i. That permutation of `Fin (1 + |t|)` sorts the concatenation of the increasing enumerations of {i} and t. Its sign is the shuffle sign that the docstring describes.

The library's next lemma proves that for i ∈ s this sign equals (−1)^{#{j∈s : j<i}}. That is the standard sign for moving i to the front, so the definition matches its docstring.

When i ∉ s, the docstring only promises "the singleton followed by s.erase i", and the definition gives exactly that. The value is still meaningful there, since it is the sign of inserting i into s.

The only structure needed is a linear order on the index type, so the generality is right. The `R`, `M` variables in scope are not used.

Mathlib has no named definition of this particular insertion sign. It does have the general building block `permOfDisjoint`, which this definition specializes to a singleton by design. That is a specific instance, not a narrowing of a general notion.
